title: Udbetaling Danmark's fraud-control models produced 135, 36 and 72 cases with benefits stopped or reduced in 2023; Amnesty International contests their effectiveness
summary: UDK/ATP ML fraud models (about 60 since 2019): 2023 figures of 135, 36 and 72 cases with revenue from three models; Amnesty (Nov 2024) calls their effectiveness questionable.
account: Udbetaling Danmark (UDK), the Danish public authority that has centralized welfare payments since 2012, has its benefits administered by ATP (Arbejdsmarkedets Tillaegspension), which designs the fraud-control components of UDK's Joint Data Unit (Den Faelles Dataenhed, established 2014 per the University of Copenhagen's Offentlig AI database) with NNIT A/S as supplier. As of 2019 UDK was reported to use up to 60 algorithms for fraud detection and other purposes; the registry describes profiling and machine learning (it names Naive Bayes classification and cluster analysis) run on linked register data. In a letter to Amnesty International before November 2024, UDK supplied its 2023 statistics for three data-driven controls: the 'Really Single' model produced 412 requested cases, 292 established control cases and 135 cases with revenue (benefits stopped or reduced); 'Model Abroad' (unreported departures, state and disability pension) 511, 351 and 36; and the parental-leave controls including the 'Fictitious Employment' model 491, 207 and 72. UDK cautioned that cases with revenue in a year are not necessarily a proportion of cases established that year. A UDK/ATP control official told Amnesty the team manages 5,000 to 6,000 cases a year of which around 1,800 come from the models. Amnesty's report of 12 November 2024 concludes that it is questionable whether the algorithms are effective, that most opened cases end with no further action, and that the system risks discrimination and mass surveillance; a Copenhagen Municipality control official said that more often than not there is no fraud in the cases UDK sends. Background sources give earlier yields: AlgorithmWatch (2020) reports that 2017 and 2018 controls unveiled about half a billion kroner in erroneous payments, and the Automating Society 2020 Denmark chapter cites a July 2019 report counting 705 cases in 2017 and 1,094 in 2018 where payments were stopped, adjusted or repaid, out of 2.7 million screened beneficiaries. The earlier verifier's dm.dk FOI report (October 2024: nearly all 1.2 million pensioners screened, only 36 cases in 2023 ending with a benefit stopped or reduced, a figure consistent with the Model Abroad row) and ATP's page attributing 260 million kr. a year of savings to IT modernization generally were not re-fetched here. The 2023 figures carry no day; the date used is the publication date of the Amnesty report that reproduces them.
purpose: Built to flag benefit recipients at elevated risk of receiving unentitled payments for manual control by UDK's control team; the recorded outcome, cases with benefits stopped or reduced, is that purpose.
system: Udbetaling Danmark / ATP Den Faelles Dataenhed fraud-control models (about 60 profiling and machine-learning models as of 2019, including 'Really Single', 'Model Abroad' and 'Fictitious Employment')
developer: ATP (Arbejdsmarkedets Tillaegspension) with NNIT A/S as supplier, for Udbetaling Danmark
deployer: Udbetaling Danmark (public authority), administered by ATP
domain: Public administration: social benefits fraud control
taxonomy_note: Closest fit: the claimed benefit is recovery or prevention of erroneous welfare payments. The only outcome figures are UDK's own statements reproduced in an Amnesty International report that contests the system; no amounts recovered for 2023 and no independent evaluation were fetched. The dm.dk FOI report and the ATP page named by the earlier verifier were not re-fetched.

ratings.reason: No individual beneficiary of the controls is identified; the people directly affected are those investigated, and by Amnesty's reading of UDK's figures 54% to almost 90% of opened cases per model ended with no further action.

UDK's own 2023 figures: 135, 36 and 72 cases with revenue from three models against 412, 511 and 491 requested cases; no amounts are given and the authority says yearly figures are not directly comparable.

Controls cover about 2.4 million recipients paid around DKK 241 billion in 2021, but the documented yield is a few hundred cases a year and Amnesty's report disputes the necessity and proportionality of the processing.

ai_role.statement: The models select 'requested cases' that UDK's HOK control team screens and investigates; decisions to stop or reduce benefits are taken by humans after investigation, and UDK measures model quality by the share of cases the team accepts for manual processing. Every outcome figure is a UDK statement (FOI responses and a letter) as reproduced verbatim in Amnesty International's report, not an official publication fetched directly; Amnesty contests effectiveness and alleges discrimination risks, and UDK rejected parts of Amnesty's assessment. NNIT built the models to ATP's specifications; no developer-authored source was fetched. The earlier verifier's dm.dk and ATP sources were not re-fetched.

produced_by: Register linkage of benefits data with civil, housing, business, tax, income, health and employment registers under a 2015 legal authorization
About 60 profiling and machine-learning models developed by NNIT to ATP's specifications
A UDK/ATP control team (HOK) that manually screens model output into established control cases and investigates them
A legal duty to also process all externally reported cases, which the control team says limits the share drawn from the models to about 30%
must_hold: Legal basis for register linkage and model use remains in force despite Amnesty's challenge and the dispute over classification under the EU AI Act
Control-team capacity of about 5,000 to 6,000 cases a year
Models continue to be monitored on their training cases, since UDK documents no evaluation metrics
Political tolerance of the system after the November 2024 criticism
